questions.text: What distinguishes a vision-language-action model from a model that only answers visual questions?

options.A: It discards visual input and operates only on transcribed instructions.
options.B: It maps visual observations and language instructions to action outputs.
options.C: It generates image captions without any action representation.
options.D: It guarantees every predicted action is physically valid without control checks.

questions.explanation: A VLA consumes observations and instructions and produces actions or action representations, rather than only descriptive text.

questions.text: A 10-dimensional action uses one discrete token per dimension at each 30 Hz control step. How many action tokens per second must be produced?
questions.explanation: 10 tokens per step ×30 steps per second =300 action tokens per second, before any other overhead.

questions.text: discretize uses idx=int((a+1)/2*(bins-1)), then clips idx to [0,bins-1]. What does discretize([-1, 0, 1], bins=5) return?
questions.explanation: The normalized values map to 0,2,4 using bins−1=4, all within the clipping range.
